key_idea: Elements never moved keep their relative order and must be exactly a prefix of the sorted array, so the answer is N minus the longest prefix of the sorted array that appears as a subsequence.
sketch: Sort a copy of the array. Scan the original once with a pointer j into the sorted copy and advance j whenever a[i]==sorted[j]; the kept elements are sorted[0..j-1] and every other element is appended once, in increasing order. Answer is N-j, O(N log N) per set. Duplicates need no special care because equal values are interchangeable and greedy matching is optimal. Input is wrapped 10 values per line, so just read tokens.
